newsitem.title: MEXICO: PRI backers stone car of Mexico City challenger.
newsitem.headline: PRI backers stone car of Mexico City challenger.

text.p: Hundreds of supporters of Mexico's ruling party, some hurling rocks the size of bowling balls, confronted an opposition politician as he campaigned in Mexico City on Thursday before key midterm elections.

Jorge Gonzalez Torres, the candidate of the Mexican Green Ecology Party (PVEM) for mayor of Mexico City, scrapped a planned visit to a city garbage dump when his campaign motorcade was attacked by supporters of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI).
"The PRI has these people worried, pressured and exploited, and it sends them out to do these kinds of things," Gonzalez Torres told reporters.

Television images showed an angry crowd of about 500 people chasing Gonzalez's car as it neared the Santa Catarina garbage dump in the eastern part of the city, one of the world's largest and most polluted.

Chanting pro-PRI slogans and waving PRI banners, some in the group threw rocks and rotten fruit at Gonzalez's car, smashing its rear window. Members of the group said they belonged to a pro-PRI union of garbage pickers and expressed support for PRI candidate Alfredo del Mazo.
The race for mayor is the first ever in Mexico City. Until now the post was considered so important that Mexico's president filled it by appointment.
Gonzalez's party has gained ground in recent months by attacking the government, rising to fourth in surveys, with about 7 percent support. Gonzalez is a former government official.
